picked.t: Central Group, controlled by Thai billionaire family Chirathivat, mulls $1.5B Vietnam investment
picked.body: "This is a particularly important market for us," Wallaya Chirathivat, chairwoman of Central Group, said during a press briefing on Thursday. Central Group entered Vietnam through Central Retail in 2012, and owns a range of retail brands, including GO!, Tops Market, Lan Chi Mart, and Supersports. It currently has 330 stores and shopping malls in 26 provinces and cities. It has invested $1.5 billion in Vietnam so far. Its plans to double that investment is driven by three main factors, the first being the country's rapid economic growth with GDP growing at 8-10% annually, outperforming the regional average, according to Chirathivat. Vietnam's population has surpassed 100 million, much larger than Thailand's, with consumers willing to shop through modern retail channels, she added. The economy also has a broad geographic structure stretching all the way from north to south, offering room for development across provinces and cities, she said. "We have cooperation agreements with Sun Group and other local businesses to research and develop projects," she said, referring to one of Vietnam's leading resort developers known for building landmarks and theme parks. Olivier Langlet, CEO of Central Retail Vietnam, said the investment plan would focus primarily on retail and shopping malls along with hotels. The company has identified 200 locations in urban areas for further study, he said. "Our team is very busy looking for suitable locations and land plots to develop projects. This is a very large workload." In the hotel business, in addition to the 984-room Centara Mirage Resort Mui Ne in Lam Dong, which has been operating since 2020, the company is developing two more properties in China-bordering Quang Ninh city, which will add about 1,000 rooms. Langlet said one challenge facing the proposal is that land in Vietnam has become "very expensive," requiring the company to carefully calculate its investments to ensure returns meet shareholders' expectations. Besides, while Vietnam has greatly simplified administrative procedures, it needs further improvements since some regulations remain ambiguous, making it difficult for investors to navigate through them. Central Retail's revenues in Vietnam in the first half of the year were more than 24 billion Thai baht (US$722 million), according to its financial report. This accounted for 20% of the company's overall revenues, making Vietnam its second largest market after Thailand. The Chirathivat family ranked fourth in Thailand's 50 Richest list compiled by Forbes this year. It has been in the list for nine years in a row.

picked.t: 3 dead, 16,000 homes flooded as heavy rain batters northern Vietnam
picked.body: As of 5:30 p.m. on Sept. 17, three people had been killed by a landslide in Da Bac Commune, Phu Tho Province. Four houses collapsed in Thanh Hoa Province, while 29 others were damaged. Another 16,310 houses were inundated, including 8,419 in Thanh Hoa, 4,787 in Ninh Binh, 2,204 in Hanoi, 749 in Nghe An and 151 in Phu Tho. The floods also submerged and damaged 22,499 ha of rice, crops and vegetables, along with 2,172 ha of other crops. A further 1,175.62 ha of aquaculture areas were affected. Some 1,999 m of irrigation canals were eroded or damaged, while 15 schools were flooded. Two incidents were reported on the dyke system, including erosion along a section of the left-bank of the Day River dyke in Ninh Binh and the overtopping of 1.4 km of dykes and embankments in Xuan Mai and Kieu Phu communes of Hanoi. Local authorities have mobilized forces to deal with the incidents. Heavy rain and landslides have also disrupted transport. Eleven landslide sites have blocked national and provincial roads, including four on National Highway 15C and three on National Highway 217. Another 30 locations have been inundated, causing traffic congestion. The Hanoi-Ho Chi Minh City railway was submerged by about 1 meter between Bim Son and Do Len, forcing passengers to be transported by road through the flooded section. The National Steering Committee for Civil Defense has asked ministries, sectors and localities to closely monitor developments and take proactive measures against heavy rain, floods, flash floods and landslides, particularly in Hanoi, Ninh Binh, Thanh Hoa and Phu Tho. Affected localities have been instructed to urgently address the aftermath, monitor river levels, enhance warnings about rapidly rising floodwaters and deep inundation, and evacuate residents from areas at risk of flooding, flash floods and landslides. Authorities have also been asked to maintain 24-hour duty to ensure timely information and coordination in disaster response. The meteorological agency urged local authorities to review vulnerable locations and potential flow obstructions and take timely preventive measures.

picked.t: Australia to exempt Vietnamese students from ban on bringing family members
picked.body: Australian Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke on Sept. 17 announced new measures that will limit accompanying family members for most student and post-study work visa holders, a crackdown on "visa hopping" by tightening rules on switching courses and visa types to extend stays, apply "No Further Stay" conditions to visitor visas, and prioritize visa applications for skilled workers in industries with labor shortages. Speaking to Vietnam News Agency in Sydney, Brian Quang Dinh, Director of Edunetwork Australia, said the key message from the latest changes was that Australia still needs international students and skilled workers, but wanted to ensure temporary visas are used for their intended purposes. He said Burke’s announcement specifies that ASEAN countries and Pacific island nations, along with certain groups of students such as PhD candidates, would be exempt from some of the new restrictions. Vietnamese passport holders are currently among those allowed to continue bringing family members, subject to applicable conditions. Based on the figures she has been monitoring, Tran said the student visa grant rate for Vietnamese applicants remains relatively positive compared with the overall picture, while Australian universities value the study attitudes and quality of many Vietnamese students. Drawing on her direct experience supporting Vietnamese students, she noted that the ability to bring family members along was one of the factors that made Australia an attractive destination for many postgraduate students. Both experts said the new adjustments should not be interpreted as meaning that Australia is no longer welcoming international students. Another notable feature of the latest reforms is that while Australia is tightening some temporary visa streams, it is giving greater priority to skilled workers in sectors facing labor shortages. According to the government announcement, sectors prioritized for skilled visa processing include healthcare, construction, education, law enforcement, defense, resources, agriculture, aquaculture and fisheries. Certain occupations in construction, healthcare and teaching have been given the highest priority. Tran mentioned that this approach could open up more opportunities for Vietnamese students and professionals with the right qualifications. It could benefit not only recent graduates but also former Vietnamese students who studied in Australia and have since returned to Vietnam, as long as they meet the requirements for the relevant skilled visa streams. Overall, the views indicate that the Sept. 17 changes do not alter the reality that Australia continues to need international students and skilled migrant workers. The major change lies in how the country selects and manages migration flows: limiting pathways primarily aimed at extending stays, while directing international students and workers more towards skills that the economy genuinely needs. For Vietnamese students, this creates greater pressure to prepare more thoroughly and develop clearer study plans, while also opening opportunities for those with relevant professional skills, clear career goals and the ability to adapt to Australia's rapidly evolving migration policies.

picked.t: 베트남, ‘두리안값’ 최고 30% 큰 폭 반등…견조한 수요 속 공급 감소 영향
picked.body: 호치민시의 한 디저트 가게에서 판매 중인 두리안. 최근 몇 달간 풍부한 공급에 급락세를 보였던 두리안 가격이 큰 폭으로 반등했다. 업계에 따르면, 일부 창고에서 거래되는 고급 두리안의 가격은 kg당 10만 동까지 치솟았다. 이전과 비교하면 20~30% 상승한 수준이다. 업계에 따르면 두리안 주산지인 닥락성(Dak Lak) 일부 저장창고에서는 선별된 고급 몬통 두리안이 kg당 10만~10만5,000동(3.9~4달러)에 거래되고 있다. 등급별로는 A급 두리안이 9만~9만5,000동(3.5~3.7달러), B급이 6만~7만 동(2.3~2.7달러)으로 지난달보다 20~30% 오른 상태다. 5월 초부터 풍부한 공급에 창고가 kg당 6만 동, 산지가는 4만5,000~5만 동(1.7~1.9달러)까지 떨어지며 수개월간 약세를 보였던 두리안 가격은 중부 고원 외 지역에서 수확이 끝나자 다시금 강한 반등을 나타내고 있다. 최근 몇 주 사이 두리안 가격 급등은 주로 공급이 감소한 데 기인했다. 업계에 따르면, 닥락성에서 수확이 한창인 가운데 농가별 수확량은 고르지 않으며, 악천후로 인해 일부 수확물은 품질 기준을 충족하지 못해 고급 두리안 공급이 감소세를 보이고 있다. 이러한 가운데 중국의 두리안 수요 증가는 가격 상승세를 부추기고 있다. 닥락성두리안협회는 “수출업체들이 중국의 중추절과 국경절(10월 1일)을 앞두고 물량 확보전에 나서고 있다. 시장 공급이 부족해지면서 두리안 가격도 상승세를 나타내고 있다”고 설명했다. 그러나 예상 수확량이 아직 상당한 만큼, 추가적으로 큰 폭의 상승세는 제한적일 것으로 예상된다. 협회에 따르면, 현재 닥락성 수확량은 전체 생산량의 약 40% 수준에 그치며, 11월 중하순까지 안정적인 공급이 이어질 전망이다. 올해 닥락성 두리안 생산량은 약 50만 톤에 달할 것으로 예상된다. 이는 전년 대비 약 20% 증가한 것으로, 수확철 후반 수요와 실제 수확량에 따라 두리안 가격은 지속적인 변동세를 나타낼 전망이다. 협회는 “수확철 후반부로 갈수록 계속되는 비가 두리안 품질에 영향을 줄 수 있다”며 “각 농가는 가격 변동에 대비해 안정적인 구매력을 갖춘 신뢰할 수 있는 수출업체와의 계약을 우선시해야 할 것”이라고 조언했다.

picked.t: 베트남, ‘투숙객’ 미신고 시 숙박시설에 과태료 부과…최대 1,200만 동
picked.body: 기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 베트남이 투숙객의 숙박 사실을 신고하지 아니한 숙박 업체에 대한 제재를 강화했다. 규정에 따른 투숙객 신고 규정을 위반한 업체는 미신고 투숙객 수에 따라 최대 1,200만 동의 과태료를 부과받을 수 있다. 지난 15일부터 시행된 정부 시행령 제347/2026/ND-CP호는 이전 시행령(282/2025/ND-CP)에 명시된 숙박시설 등록·관리 위반에 관한 새로운 제재를 담고 있다. 이번 시행령에 포함된 새 규정에 따르면, △숙박업체 △공동주택 △의료시설 △관광숙박시설 △산업단지 내 숙박시설 △기타 숙박 관련 시설 등은 투숙객의 숙박 사실을 신고하지 않을 경우, 미신고 인원 수에 따라 과태료가 차등 부과된다. 구체적으로 미신고 인원이 1~3명일 경우, 과태료는 200만~400만 동(77~154달러)이며, 4~8명은 400만~800만 동(154~308달러)의 과태료가 부과된다. 9명 이상인 경우 과태료는 800만 동에서 최대 1,200만 동(462달러)에 이를 수 있다. 투숙객 신고 관련 규정에 따르면, 각 숙박시설 및 업체는 투숙객 도착 시 관할 거주등록기관에 투숙 사실을 신고해야 한다. 신고 내용으로는 △성명 △생년월일 △공민번호 또는 여권번호 △투숙 목적 △투숙 기간 △투숙지 주소 등이 포함된다. 투숙 신고는 투숙객 도착일 오후 11시 이전에 완료돼야 하며, 이를 넘겨 도착하는 경우, 익일 오전 8시까지 신고해야 한다. 이 밖에도 숙박시설 관리와 관련된 일부 행정위반 사항은 과태료 외 규정에 따라 추가적인 제재가 뒤따를 수 있어 주의가 필요하다.

picked.t: 베트남, 국제유가 상승에 ‘휘발유값’ 리터당 2.5만 동 돌파…4개월 만에 최고치
picked.body: 베트남 호치민시 한 주유소에서 주유 중인 시민. 국제 에너지 가격 상승 여파로 인해 베트남의 휘발유 가격이 리터(L)당 2만5,000동(96센트)을 넘어섰다. 이로써 베트남 휘발유 소매가는 지난 5월 중순 이후 최고치까지 올랐다. 베트남 공상부와 재무부 간 조정위원회는 17일 석유제품 최고가격을 L당 5.12~5.86% 범위로 상향 조정했다. 국제 유가가 상승한 데 따른 영향이다. 이날 최고가격 조정으로 유종별 L당 소매가 상한은 △E10휘발유(E10 RON 95-III) 2만5,630동(1달러) +5.78% △E5휘발유(E5 RON 92) 2만5,130동(97센트) +5.86% △경유 2만9,940동(1.2달러) +5.12% 등으로 조정됐다. 최근 국제 유가는 중동 지역 후티 반군과 사우디아라비아 간 분쟁 격화, 미국 연방준비제도(Fed)의 기준금리 인상 등으로 큰 변동을 보였다. 이로 인해 국제 연료 가격은 이전 조정 주기와 비교해 두 자릿수 상승세를 나타냈다. 휘발유(RON95) 가격은 10.6% 올라 배럴당 146.2달러를, 경유 가격은 182.6달러로 13.4% 상승했다. 이는 지난 4월 초 이후 최고치로, 미국과 이란 간 분쟁이 재점화되기 전과 비교하면 유종별 가격은 28~41% 상승한 수준이다. 올해 초 기준 베트남 내 석유 도매업체는 모두 33곳으로, 이 중에는 항공유만 취급하는 5개사와 응이선(Nghi Son)·융꿧(Dung Quat)정유공장 등을 운영하는 빈선정유화학(Binh Son Refining and Petrochemical)이 포함된다.
